```{r echo = FALSE, message=FALSE}
require(remotes)
remotes::install_github("rowlandseymour/speedyBBT", ref = "player_item")
require(knitr)
```

## Introduction 

+ Comparative judgment data collected using pairwise item comparison
+ `speedyBBT` package fits Bayesian Bradley-Terry models to the data
+ New version of `speedyBBT` provides more helper functions to process output
+ `pkgdown` website to support users with additional documentation

## Terms

+ Items for comparison are called "items"
+ The outcome of a comparison is called a "win" or "loss"
+ Estimated parameters are called "qualities" of the players/items - $\lambda$
+ Many options for model-fitting including priors and formulas for player/item-specific advantages

## Structure of data items

```{r}
#| echo: TRUE
library(speedyBBT)
names(forcedMarriage)
```

```{r}
#| echo: TRUE
#| table-caption: "First 5 rows of the forcedMarriage comparisons dataset"
kable(forcedMarriage$comparisons[1:5, ])
```

## Adjacency matrix

+ This is a square matrix with rows and columns corresponding to the players/items
+ We assume adjacent items are more similar than non-adjacent items
+ Can be used for prior variance

```{r}
#| echo: TRUE
#| table-caption: "Upper left of the adjacency matrix for the forcedMarriage dataset"
kable(forcedMarriage$adjacencyMatrix[1:5,1:5] )
```

# Model fitting functions

## Model options

+ Several forms of Bayesian Bradley-Terry model 
+ `speedyBBTm` uses Polyá-Gamma latent variables to improve speed
+ `BBTm.ties` allows for ties in comparisons
+ `BBTm` allows for comparison-specific and player-specific advantages 

## Using a model fitting function

```{r}
#| echo: TRUE
expA <- expm::expm(forcedMarriage$adjacencyMatrix)
prior.var <- diag(diag(expA)^-0.5) %*% expA %*% diag(diag(expA)^-0.5)

set.seed(432)

forcedMarriageModel <- speedyBBTm(
  outcome = rep(1, length(forcedMarriage$comparisons$win)),
  item1 = forcedMarriage$comparisons$win,
  item2 = forcedMarriage$comparisons$lost,
  item.prior.var = prior.var,
  n.iter = 1000,
  burn.in = 100
)
```

## If your data includes an advantage

```{r}
#| echo: TRUE
wimbledonModel <- BBTm(
  outcome = wimbledon$matches$outcome,
  item2 = wimbledon$matches$loser,
  item1 = wimbledon$matches$winner,
  advantage = wimbledon$matches$secondWeek,
  formula = ~ rank + points,
  data = wimbledon$players,
  n.iter = 10, burn.in = 1, verbose = FALSE
)
```

## `plot_abilities` function

```{r}
#| echo: TRUE
quality_table <- plot_qualities(forcedMarriageModel, player_names = forcedMarriage$wards$NAME)
```

## Parameter helper functions

+ `parameter()` returns a vector of posterior samples for a given parameter
```{r}
#| echo: TRUE
#| fig-alt: "Posterior distribution of lambda"
lambda <- parameter(forcedMarriageModel, "lambda", c(10,20))
hist(lambda, main = "Posterior distribution of lambda", xlab = "lambda")
```

## Integration with `{bayesplot}`

+ allows for easy plotting of posterior distributions and diagnostics

```{r}
#| echo: TRUE
#| fig-alt: "Posterior distributions of lambda[10], lambda[20], lambda[30], lambda[40], and alpha.sq"
library(bayesplot)
bayesplot::mcmc_dens(forcedMarriageModel, pars = c("lambda[10]", "lambda[20]", "lambda[30]", "lambda[40]", "alpha.sq"))
```
